# Genesis Apocryphon Column 21 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Genesis Apocryphon Column 21 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 21:1 — "afflicting spirit" / "tormenting spirit"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "an-afflicting-spirit" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "an afflicting spirit" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "a tormenting spirit" | Dynamic; intensifies |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "an afflicting spirit." The Aramaic root speaks of affliction; "tormenting" adds intensity not warranted.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:3 — "know her" / "be intimate with her"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "nor-did-he-know-her" | Literal; biblical euphemism |
| LOGOS | "nor know her" | Formal; preserves euphemism |
| PNEUMA | "or be intimate with her" | Dynamic; clarifies euphemism |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "nor know her." The biblical euphemism of "knowing" for sexual relations is well understood and should be preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:6 — "magicians" / "sorcerers"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-magicians" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "the magicians" | Formal; echoes Exodus 7-8 |
| PNEUMA | "the sorcerers" | Dynamic; different English term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "the magicians." This term echoes the Exodus narrative (where Egyptian magicians also fail) and creates an important intertextual link.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:10 — "afflicted them all" / "struck them all down"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "afflicted-them-all" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "afflicted them all" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "struck them all down too" | Dynamic; more violent imagery |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. "Struck down" implies death; the healers fled, indicating they were afflicted but survived.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:11 — "fled from before him" / "fled from his presence" / "fled in terror"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fled from-before-him" | Literal Aramaic idiom |
| LOGOS | "fled from his presence" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "fled in terror" | Dynamic; adds emotional note |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "fled from his presence." PNEUMA's "in terror" adds an emotion not specified in the Aramaic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:18 — "he shall live" / "the king will recover"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "and-he-shall-live" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "and the king shall live" | Formal; identifies subject |
| PNEUMA | "and the king will recover" | Dynamic; "recover" for illness context |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "and the king shall live." "Live" is the Aramaic verb; "recover" weakens the life-death stakes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 21:22 — "Restore" / "Give back" / "send away"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Restore Sarai" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "Restore Sarai" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "Give Sarai back" | Dynamic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET rendering "Restore." The formal term carries appropriate weight for the return of a patriarch's wife.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 21:28/30 — "rebuked" / "driven from"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "may-be-rebuked" / "was-rebuked" | Literal rendering of Aramaic |
| LOGOS | "may be rebuked" / "was rebuked" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "will be driven away" / "was driven out" | Dynamic; exorcistic language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted PNEUMA's "driven from/out." The context is explicitly exorcistic (laying on of hands, departure of an evil spirit), and "driven out" is the standard English for exorcism. "Rebuked" understates the action.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of PNEUMA.

---

## 21:34 — "gave her" / "showered her with gifts"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "gave-her" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "gave her" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "showered her with gifts" | Dynamic; emphasizes generosity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "gave her." PNEUMA's "showered with gifts" is idiomatic but anachronistic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 9*
*Resolution: LOGOS 7, PNEUMA 1, EMET 0, Compromise 1*
